transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
- Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
President Trump criticized Ukrainian President
Volodymyr Zelensky today, the latest in a series
of Trump's actions and policies favoring Russia
in recent weeks.
- Frankly, Zelensky is not helping matters much.
I think he doesn't want to stop it,
but I want to see people not die.
They're losing probably on average 25 to 35,000 soldiers
every single month.
All I want to do, I don't care, I want to get the worst up.
- Last week, Trump waved sanctions on Moscow,
limited Ukraine's use of SpaceX's Starlink system
for battlefield operations and made a deal
to import Russian diesel fuel.
Trump said today he would be willing to meet
with Russian President Volodymyr Putin
and China's Xi Jinping when he visits China next month.
- President Trump has endorsed Israeli Prime Minister
Benjamin Netanyahu in his bid for reelection next week.
As NPR's Daniel Estrin reports Netanyahu's now promising
Israeli voters if he's reelected,
he and Trump will target Iran.
- Trump said on social media he may soon need Israel's help
to quote, "Finish the job in Iran,"
and that only Netanyahu would help.
Trump's endorsement is a major boost for Netanyahu.
Israeli elections are being held next week,
and Netanyahu is trailing in the polls
against the opposition front-runner Gadi Isinkot.
Netanyahu released a campaign video saying
if he's reelected, he'll quote,
"Destroy the Iranian threat and he'll have two years
"to do it," he says, while Trump is still in office.
A person briefed on the matter not authorized
to speak publicly told NPR, Trump and Netanyahu
have discussed the possibility of a new attack on Iran.
Daniel Estrin, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
- President Trump has directed the federal government
to bolster research into women's health,
a move pushed by First Lady Melania Trump.
The executive order creates a women's health division
at the National Institutes of Health,
and it creates a White House task force.
Melania Trump says the effort will change
the reality of women's health.
Overnight curfews have been put in place
in parts of France after riots over the weekend.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports Prime Minister
Sebastian Le Corneux gave local authorities
the power to impose such curfews
to counter what he calls delinquents and thugs.
The curfew includes Paris's Place de la République,
a central gathering point that has seen
some of the worst skirmishes between protesters and police,
as well as disruption and looting.
The mayor of Nice announced a curfew
specifically for young people.
There are also restrictions in some northern cities,
including Lille, which saw its town hall
broken into over the weekend.
President Emmanuel Macron and his government
are being blamed for the mayhem.
Far-right leader Marine Le Pen said the interior minister
was not prepared and should resign.
The prime minister says ultra-left radical groups
are trying to create chaos
ahead of the next presidential election.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Paris.
-The S&P 500 rose 4/10 of a percent today,
but the majority of U.S. stocks outside of AI
and tech stocks fell.
This is "NPR News."
Mississippi's attorney general says a police officer
in the town of Cenotobia was justified in using force
in the June shooting death of a one-year-old boy.
Cohen Wiley was killed as officers responded
to a shoplifting call at a local Walmart
where they saw Cohen, his mother, and her friend
leave the store and begin driving away.
The Mississippi Bureau of Investigation
said their vehicle drove toward law enforcement,
at which point an officer opened fire.
Cohen's mother disputes that claim.
Artificial intelligence has gotten very good
at tracking the paths of hurricanes in the Atlantic Ocean,
but it needs improvement in the Pacific.
From member station WUSF, Jessica Mazaros reports.
-Google DeepMind's AI model was spot-on
about Hurricane Isaias's path in the Gulf
while missing the mark for Hurricane Simon
in the Eastern Pacific.
Brian McNoldy, a hurricane researcher
at the University of Miami,
says AI doesn't use complicated math and science
the way conventional prediction models do.
-It makes us a little uncomfortable
because we like to know why you're getting the right answer,
and I feel like we don't, or at least I don't.
-AI creates forecasts based on patterns
from thousands of past storms and atmospheric data.
Forecasters say Google DeepMind's projection
for storm strength also needs some work.
For "NPR News," I'm Jessica Mazaros in Tampa, Florida.
-Japan is launching a spacecraft
to bring back samples from Phobos,
one of the Martian moons.
Scientists hope the five-year mission
will reveal how the moon formed,
potentially shedding light on the origins of life
in the solar system.
The mission aims to return to Earth in 2031.
This is "NPR News."
-This message comes from Charles Schwab
with their original podcast "Choiceology,"
hosted by Katie Milkman,
an award-winning behavioral scientist
and author of the best-selling book "How to Change."
"Choiceology" is a show about the psychology and economics
behind people's decisions.
Hear true stories from Nobel laureates, historians,
authors, athletes, and more about how to make better decisions
to help avoid costly mistakes.
Download the latest episode and subscribe
at Schwab.com/podcast or wherever you listen.

topics.text: Trump criticizes Zelensky, says he doesn't want to stop the war in Ukraine
Trump endorses Netanyahu's reelection bid, Netanyahu vows to target Iran if reelected
Trump directs federal government to boost women's health research, creates NIH division and task force
Overnight curfews imposed in parts of France, including Paris and Nice, after weekend riots
S&P 500 rises slightly while most U.S. stocks outside AI and tech decline
Mississippi attorney general says police were justified in fatal shooting of one-year-old in Cenotobia
AI weather models excel at Atlantic hurricane tracks but lag in Eastern Pacific, researchers say
Japan launches spacecraft to return samples from Mars moon Phobos by 2031
